name: brand-identity
body: kalide has a documented visual identity, currently absent from the repo (no `logo/`/brand directory or brand SVG exists anywhere today): a hexagonal faceted mark with an orange triangular accent; a wordmark "kalide" set in Inter, lowercase-only; a three-colour palette — "the void" `#0F1115`, "the structure" `#F8F9FA`, "the enforcer" `#FF5722` (hex values as given on the brand board; documented here as the approved decision, not derived or guessed beyond what was supplied); the mark scalable/exported at 512, 128, 32 and 16px. The brand board exists only as an image, so the SVG is a hand-authored recreation from it (close to the board, not a pixel-identical trace), with the wordmark text outlined to paths; the PNGs are rendered from that SVG. It lives as plain repository files under the repo-root `brand/` directory, referenced only from documentation and marketing surfaces — README hero image, package-channel (Homebrew/Scoop) descriptions, an optional GitHub social-preview image — never embedded in the binary. The brand is all rights reserved, not Apache-2.0: `brand/LICENSE` reads "Copyright © Really Knows AI. All rights reserved." plus the statement that "kalide" and the kalide logo are trademarks of Really Knows AI and are not licensed under Apache-2.0. A repo-root `TRADEMARKS.md` gives a short permitted-use policy: anyone may refer to kalide by name and use the unmodified logo to link to or refer to the project; no one may use the name or logo for forks or derived products, use modified logos, or use them in a way implying endorsement. AC: `brand/` holds a committed hand-authored SVG of the mark and wordmark whose palette hex values match those recorded here; the wordmark is outlined to paths (no `<text>` element or font reference), so it renders without a system Inter install; the PNGs at 512/128/32/16px are exports of that committed SVG; `brand/LICENSE` exists with the all-rights-reserved and trademark statements; `TRADEMARKS.md` exists at the repo root with the permitted-use policy above; `brand/` contains no third-party artwork (e.g. the Go gopher, CC BY 4.0 by Renée French — if ever used in docs it lives outside `brand/` with attribution); no file under `internal/assets` or any `go:embed` directive references the brand files.
